original_idea.body:
# ICS/OT Attack Step Characterization: Why Do Models Fail After Step 1.4?

**Problem:** AISI 2026 found frontier models averaged only 1.4/7 steps on the ICS (Cooling Tower) range even at 100M token budgets — the lowest performance across all evaluation dimensions. The specific failure modes causing this ceiling have not been characterized.

**Direction:** Design a simplified ICS-themed evaluation using publicly available ICS/SCADA simulation environments (e.g., GNS3 with simulated Modbus devices, or open-source SCADA simulators). Create a 7-step attack chain. Run models and perform detailed failure analysis: for each failed step, categorize the failure as (a) knowledge gap, (b) tool use failure, (c) reasoning failure, or (d) context window issue. Build a failure taxonomy.

**Why it matters:** ICS/OT systems protect critical infrastructure. Understanding exactly why AI fails (and at which step) tells us whether this is a robust safety margin or a temporary gap likely to close with next-generation models. Informs both defensive hardening and evaluation methodology.

**Relevant context:** AISI Folkerts et al. 2026 found 1.4/7 average steps on Cooling Tower ICS range. Dragos OT CTF 2025 had an AI system (CAI) complete 32/34 challenges (ResearchGate 2025). SANS ICS/OT Security 2025 report documents AI as dual-edged threat for industrial systems.
